acvp_ref_note: Upstream ACVP-Server ref this attestation was generated against (immutable NIST release tag v1.1.0.42, published 2026-04-16, upstream commit 15c0f3d...). The per-algorithm source_url entries below embed this ref as a human-browseable URL that resolves to the exact attested bytes. .github/workflows/acvp_validation.yml sets ACVP_REF to the same tag and fails the build if this field, the workflow env var, and the value nist_vectors/fetch_vectors.py actually used (recorded in nist_vectors/validation_summary.json::acvp_ref) ever disagree. When refreshing this attestation against a newer ACVP-Server release, update this field, every source_url below, the workflow's ACVP_REF default, and nist_vectors/fetch_vectors.py::DEFAULT_ACVP_REF in the same commit; if the per-algorithm vector counts change with the new snapshot, also update totals and EXPECTED_VECTORS.

total_vectors_skipped_note: total_vectors_skipped = total_vectors_skipped_aft_filtered + total_vectors_skipped_non_aft (5789 = 4667 + 1122). The AFT-filtered bucket (run_vectors.py::results.summary.total_skipped, aggregated from per-algorithm vectors_skipped) counts individual vectors filtered out within AFT test groups: non-byte-aligned inputs, non-target parameter sets, and ML-DSA/SLH-DSA internal/pre-hash test groups. The non-AFT bucket counts entire test groups with testType != 'AFT' that are skipped wholesale (LDT + VOT + the ML-KEM-1024 EncapDecap groups in the current coverage; MCT moved OUT of this bucket in v3.0.0 when the four SHA-3 MCT runners were added, dropping the SHA-3 contribution but not the total). These are tracked per-algorithm in run_vectors.py under the legacy field name 'mct_skipped' (the field name predates MCT coverage and is now semantically a misnomer — it counts non-AFT test groups generally); the ML-KEM-1024 EncapDecap groups (encapsulation randomness parameter m not exposed by AMA) are counted there, i.e. as non-AFT, which is why they belong in this bucket and not the AFT-filtered one.
skip_categories_aft_filtered: Non-target parameter sets (ML-KEM-512/768, ML-DSA-44/87, SLH-DSA non-SHA2-256f)
ML-DSA/SLH-DSA internal and pre-hash test groups
skip_categories_non_aft: Large Data Test (LDT) groups — multi-gigabyte inputs outside the CI harness scope (8 SHA-3 tcIds)
Variable Output Test (VOT) groups — output-length coverage is already exercised by AFT vectors in the same upstream vector files (1024 SHAKE tcIds)
ML-KEM-1024 EncapDecap groups (90 tcIds — testType != 'AFT'; encapsulation randomness parameter m not exposed by AMA, so the groups are skipped wholesale)
Any other testType != 'AFT' test group encountered upstream

parameter_set_coverage_note: The `algorithms` array above is the IMMUTABLE ACVP self-attestation: 1,215 vectors against ACVP-Server release tag v1.1.0.42, reproducible byte-for-byte and gated by .github/workflows/acvp_validation.yml's EXPECTED_VECTORS floor. It is deliberately NOT extended below. `additional_validated_coverage` records the parameter sets this library also implements and validates in CI on every pull request, with each one's actual source — which is not ACVP for all of them. Merging the two would state that ML-KEM-512 is ACVP-attested when its corpus is Wycheproof's, and that ML-DSA-44 is attested against an immutable ref when its vectors were taken from ACVP-Server's mutable master branch. INVARIANT-16 (Honest Compliance and Audit Claims) forbids both. Promoting an entry from this list into the attestation proper requires an immutable upstream ref and a matching EXPECTED_VECTORS bump, in one commit.
